name: WHO emergencies
summary: WHO's Bundibugyo Ebola emergency of international concern stays in force; no new PHEIC found to 9 Nov
state: WHO's Director-General determined the Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May, and it remains in force under the Emergency Committee's second-meeting recommendations, issued on 24 Aug (WHO). WHO's 6 Nov outbreak update reports continuing transmission in DR Congo. Searches to 9 Nov found no new PHEIC in the past 30 days and no third Emergency Committee meeting announced.
for_you: WHO advises against travel or trade restrictions linked to this emergency. Travellers can follow FCDO travel advice and NaTHNaC guidance for the countries affected.
rubric_hit: A PHEIC in effect (Bundibugyo Ebola, determined 17 May): Watch. No new PHEIC in the past 30 days, so not Alert.
basis_detail: WHO (PHEIC and IHR Emergency Committee decisions)
basis_by: WHO (PHEIC and IHR Emergency Committee decisions)

sources.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya and Nigeria

why: A WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) or 'pandemic emergency' is the top official global health alarm.
drivers: Outbreak spread, IHR Emergency Committee decisions.

rubric.alert: A new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days, or a pandemic emergency declared.
rubric.watch: A PHEIC in effect, or an IHR Emergency Committee convened.
rubric.normal: No PHEIC in effect other than long-running polio.
